text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.S. Ambassador Prudence Bushnell warns famine relief food distribution should not be politicised and no one should be denied food for political reasons.
- A 8.5 billion shilling World Bank road rehabilitation project will be completed in the next two to three years.
- Students from three state universities accuse vice chancellors of compromising education standards through frequent closures.
- President Daniel arap Moi confirms the general election will be held this year.
- The opposition and the ruling Kenya African National Union party gear up for a by-election in Langata on Tuesday.
- The government begins a head count of all its employees to flush out ghost workers.
- A church minister and a local businessman are transporting refugees from the Great Lakes region to Kenya.
- President Moi accuses the opposition of propagating violence in Kenya.
- Nineteen people die in road accidents in two days. ($1=54 Kenyan Shillings)
